objective: After v11 reaches a terminal verified state, diagnose class- and subject-level errors, run a CPU-only spectral logistic-regression baseline on the identical six-subject held-out folds, select at most two pre-registered improvements from evidence, run one fresh version, and compare it fairly with v9, v11, and the baseline.
deliverables: A v11 terminal-validation and locked-TF2.4 child-verification record.
An immutable error analysis covering pooled and per-subject/class support, confusion matrices, and uncertainty limits for v9 and v11.
A CPU-only spectral logistic-regression baseline that reconstructs and verifies the exact v11 membership hashes before fitting.
A written decision record selecting no more than two training changes using only train/validation evidence.
One fresh, exactly-once improved run with its own protocol, preflight evidence, review, and terminal validation.
A final comparison that labels v9/v11/baseline/improved results as fixed-cohort preliminary evidence rather than a manuscript-equivalence claim.
nonGoals: Do not interrupt, modify, retry, resume, or relaunch v11 while it is live.
Do not select hyperparameters from held-out test subjects.
Do not make an 83 percent or manuscript-equivalence claim from the six-subject pilot.
Do not reuse an existing run namespace after a terminal outcome.
acceptance: Every baseline fold proves equality of reconstructed and v11 split membership hashes before model fitting.
Baseline features, standardization, class weights, model selection, and metrics are train/validation-only until the single test evaluation.
The improvement decision records the evidence and a fixed maximum of two modifications before its fresh launch.
Each result table includes per-class support and makes missing-class limitations explicit.
Fresh-run terminal validation and locked-TF2.4 standalone verification pass for every child, or a non-retried failure record explains why this objective cannot advance.
decisions: v11 must complete before its metrics are treated as evidence or any follow-on GPU training is admitted.
The baseline is a deterministic, CPU-only spectral logistic model so it does not contend with the live GPU run.
Feature standardization and model selection use training and validation partitions only; held-out test partitions are never used to choose the improvement.
